glosses: To make (products or services) available for sale and promote them.

examples.text: We plan to market an ecology model by next quarter.

glosses: To sell.

examples.text: We marketed more this quarter already than all last year!

glosses: To deal in a market; to buy or sell; to make bargains for provisions or goods.
To shop in a market; to attend a market.

examples.text: We did a little shopping; but I cannot remember much of the town. It was Saturday night, and all Perth was marketing.

glosses: A gathering of people for the purchase and sale of merchandise, often periodic at a set time.

examples.text: The right to hold a weekly market was an invaluable privilege not given to all towns in the Middle Ages.
There's a market every Thursday and Saturday in the town square.

examples.text: This site on North Street used to be the market, until it was redeveloped.

glosses: Any physical store selling groceries, such as a grocery store or convenience store.

examples.text: Stop by the market on your way home and pick up some milk.

Mixes [such as cake mixes, pancake mixes, or sauce mixes] are sometimes a reasonable alternative and sometimes not. […] Pancake mixes often offer no advantages at all. So you buy the mix. Only a glutton for punishment would do otherwise.

glosses: A group of potential or current customers for one's product.

examples.text: We believe that the market for the new widget will be the older homeowner.

glosses: A geographical area or region where a certain commercial demand exists.

examples.text: Foreign markets were lost as our currency rose versus their valuta.

glosses: A formally organized, sometimes monopolistic, system of trading in specified goods or effects.

examples.text: The stock market ceased to be monopolized by the paper-shuffling national stock exchanges with the advent of Internet markets.

glosses: The sum total traded in a process of individuals trading for certain commodities.
